Two quick asks up front: 1) can Redwood accept our carve for open-source dependencies where the third-party claim arises solely from a customer-modified integration; and 2) can we get clarity on notice timing — we asked for a 30-calendar-day requirement for written notice after discovery, which is tight.

I've attached a short summary (redline_comments_summary.docx) that flags our top three concerns: defense control when the claim is IP infringement, cap carveouts for willful infringement, and evidence-preservation timelines. We want to keep the commercial terms moving, but legal needs a workable path for discovery and potential litigation.

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding Novus's redlines. Key points for Legal Ops to weigh in on:

- Novus is proposing customer-notice = 30 calendar days after discovery. That is aggressively short; we typically push for notice within "reasonable prompt" or 45–60 days.
- They want an OSS modification carveout. We can probably accept for customer-modified code only if we limit to components they materially altered and require them to take primary defense for that part.
- Defense/control: They want the ability to assume defense if we don't move quickly; they also ask for a settlement carveout for amounts that don't bind Redwood.

Suggested approach: propose a middle ground — 45 days for notice in the MSA with a 30-day discovery exchange requirement in the Order Form for high-priority claims; accept OSS carveout limited to customer-modified modules (with logging/evidence requirements); maintain Redwood's right to control defense but provide an express covenant that we won't unreasonably refuse settlement that mitigates costs.

Can you draft proposed language we can send back to Novus? Also flag any insurance/escrow implications — Marissa, please weigh in on whether this elevates to a procurement credit request.

Thanks, Grace
Grace O'Connor

Grace / Karthik — I'm NovusHealth's outside counsel and looped in to respond on the indemnity language. A few points from our side:

1) Notice timing — Novus is open to 45 days if Redwood commits to a short internal escalation timeline (they want to avoid losing leverage with potential claimants).

2) Defense control — we need to preserve Customer's right to assume defense where Redwood declines to defend or if there's a conflict. We are okay with Redwood leading defense for most matters but want a clear, quick dispute path if egregious conduct is alleged.

3) OSS carveout — acceptable if the MSA requires the Customer to provide a reproducible build and a changelog showing modifications; otherwise the carveout is too broad.

I can propose redline language that implements the 45-day notice compromise, a short "meet-and-confer" bench for control disputes (7 business days), and an evidence requirement for OSS carveouts. Would you like tracked edits back into Novus's PDF or a clean markup?

Best,

Sara / Tom — thanks for the redlines and Michael for the note. Attached is our proposed compromise language as tracked edits in the MSA (also pasted below). High-level points:

- Notice: We will accept 45 calendar days from discovery for written notice in the MSA, with a duty to provide interim oral notice if the claimant requires immediate action.
- Defense/control: Redwood will retain primary defense control for third-party IP claims but Novus may assume defense if Redwood does not commence a defense within 14 business days after notice or if there is an irreconcilable conflict. If Novus assumes defense, Redwood can participate at its own expense and will remain indemnified for amounts resulting from Redwood-conducted defense. Settlement: any settlement that binds the other party requires prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld).
- OSS carveout: Carveout limited to customer-modified components where Novus provides a reproducible build, changelog, and test evidence; Novus must lead and bear costs for defense of those components.

I have included an addition requiring preservation of logs and configuration snapshots for 90 days post-notice. Also suggested a narrow insurance cooperation clause (assistance with claims notice to insurer).

Attachments: [Redwood_Proposed_MSA_redlines.pdf (PDF, 64 KB)]

If Novus can accept these points we'll prepare a short mutual amendment for signature and avoid further delay to the Order Form. Let me know if you want a call to walk through the language.

—Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Karthik — thanks for the quick turn. Novus has reviewed Redwood's proposed compromise and we can accept the 45-day notice (with interim oral flag) and the OSS carveout conditions you included. A couple of small asks before we sign:

• Can we narrow "14 business days" to 10 business days to assume defense if Redwood doesn't act? It's an operational ask — our security team wants to avoid prolonged exposure while a claim matures.
• Please make explicit that evidence preservation includes API call logs and model input snapshots (to the extent stored) — we listed those as examples in our comments.

If you can take the 10 business days and explicitly include API/model logs in the preservation list, Novus is prepared to sign the amendment and proceed with the Order Form execution this week.

Sara
